summary: Real pain (paid retries on image-to-video), but there is no named buyer, ChatGPT with a pasted guide is a free substitute, and models are fixing camera control. M1 is text-only, so it doesn't test the photo-aware claim.

demand.evidence: Camera control is unreliable in Wan 2.2 and retries cost about $0.68–$0.91 per Kling clip (stable-diffusion-art.com, marcandrews.com), but only one $19 Gumroad prompt tool exists as a paid analogue and RESEARCH.md says willingness to pay is unproven.

statusQuo.evidence: Sellers regenerate 3–4 times or paste a free guide into ChatGPT; per-clip waste is a couple of dollars, too small to justify a new subscription, and ChatGPT with an image already writes photo-aware prompts.

specificity.evidence: The buyer is a category (Etsy/Shopify sellers with 20–200 SKUs, solo agents); no named person or consequence. Hobbyists feel the pain but want it free.

wedge.evidence: One photo, one model, one camera move, one prompt is shippable in a weekend, but a template table has no moat. A curated tested prompt pack could test demand with no app.

futureFit.evidence: Models and generators are fixing camera control and adding native camera presets and built-in prompt helpers, which shrinks the problem, and templates need constant upkeep.

premises: Prompts are the main cause of failed generations (partly contradicted: model asymmetry such as pan-left yielding pan-right is not a prompt problem)
Sellers will pay for a prompt writer separately from the generator (unsupported)
A local LLM as the engine works at $0 (true for hobbyists, not for sellers who won't run Ollama)
Better prompts cut retries by at least 30% (unmeasured)
Templates stay valid as models change (doubtful)
alternatives: Minimal: a $19 one-time pack of tested per-model camera prompts with before/after clips, no app
Ideal: the full photo-aware app with history and payment from the PRD
Lateral: a free Custom GPT or browser side panel for Kling and Runway that funnels to the paid pack
No existing repo of David's covers image-to-video, so there is nothing to extend
wedge: One landing page promising camera prompts that don't pan the wrong way, with 3 hand-made before/after clips and a $9 pre-pay link.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel, two template files, seven presets, Vitest and a free-tier model. M1 takes a text description rather than a photo, so the photo-aware claim is untested until M2. The proving test is a hand-rated 30-photo comparison of attempts to an acceptable clip, plain prompt vs clipcue, which needs generator credits that David would have to pay for.

risks: ChatGPT or Claude plus a pasted guide is a good-enough free substitute
No named buyer and no proof of willingness to pay
Retry reduction may be nil if variance is in the model
Template upkeep as Wan, LTX, Kling and Runway change
Generators ship their own photo-aware prompt helpers
Real-estate use adds disclosure issues (California AB 723)
killCriteria: Drop it if a two-week test gets fewer than 5 waitlist or pre-pay signups from 50 qualified visitors, no seller can be named who spends over $10 a month on retries, the 30-photo test shows less than 30% fewer attempts, or a major generator ships photo-aware prompt suggestions.
